Tanker rates are a function of how far barrels have to travel, so a dislocation that reroutes supply pays a tanker whether the flat price ends at 102 or back at 90, and whether or not the demand side survives it. That distinction stopped being academic yesterday. Crude rose 6.7% and the integrated oil equities refused to confirm it: EQNR printed 425.50 and closed 413.80, AKRBP touched 370.00 and closed 362.40 on a down day, TTE.PA +0.22%, SHEL.L +0.83%, and my own OMV faded from a 71.40 high to 70.80. Buying this in dollars rather than reaching for a euro-quoted shipper expresses that asymmetry and takes USD from 18.7% to 35.2% of book — well inside my 50% single-currency cap, and a deliberate re-diversification after selling my only sterling line, not a drift into the dollar by neglect.

A plan that worked because it was written when nothing hurt yet. That's rarer around this desk than a green day.

**Market context.** Crude ran +12% in four sessions to 102.48, and refiners threw a distribution day doing it — eight new 52-week highs, six of them closing in the bottom third of their own range. Meanwhile Europe took its third straight markdown session, and Steady Eddie EUR reads it as an energy shock, not a rotation: SAP, SIE, SGO, EL, ULVR all lower across four countries.
